title: Moment Optimization in the Navascués-Pironio-Acín Hierarchy
authors: Francesco Flora, Losel Matos, Tim Heightman, Tamás Kriváchy, Adan Garriga, Antonio Acín
abstract: The Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy provides a convergent sequence of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations for noncommutative polynomial optimisation, ubiquitous in quantum physics. However, its practical applicability is limited by the combinatorial growth in operator moments required at each level. Since not all moments contribute equally to bound tightness, selecting moments within a fixed computational budget is a relevant problem.   We reframe moment selection as combinatorial subset selection and show it is governed by strong higher-order synergistic interactions among moments, quantified through a marginal synergy diagnostic adapted from complex systems theory. We develop and compare three optimisation methods: Parallel Tempering (PT), an RBM-based reinforcement learning policy, and Bayesian Optimisation (BO). On the $I_{3322}$ Bell inequality benchmark, all three substantially outperform greedy approaches at costs around two orders of magnitude below brute force, with the RBM achieving the closest approach to optimal throughout the hard transition regime.   We apply the framework to the 174 Bell inequalities in the $(4,4,2,2)$ scenario, finding heterogeneous convergence behaviour across inequalities, and to the one-dimensional Heisenberg spin chain, demonstrating that physically motivated monomial bases are internally compressible and are not globally optimal in general. A budget-aware search over a broader pool improves certified bounds on long-range correlations by nearly two orders of magnitude. These results establish a scalable framework for moment selection in noncommutative polynomial optimisation, with broad applications across quantum physics and quantum information.
summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck of moment optimization in the NPA hierarchy by treating moment selection as a combinatorial search problem. The authors develop and compare advanced machine learning and sampling techniques (RBM, BO) that efficiently select optimal subsets of moments. This establishes a scalable framework for obtaining tighter, certified bounds on quantum correlations and energy gaps.
main_problem: The core problem is optimizing moment selection within the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to efficiently bound solutions to noncommutative polynomial optimization problems.
main_result: The developed framework allows for scalable moment selection, significantly improving certified bounds on quantum correlations and ground-state energies by orders of magnitude compared to greedy or full brute-force methods.
method: The authors reframe moment selection as a combinatorial subset selection problem and compare three optimization techniques: Parallel Tempering (PT), RBM-based Reinforcement Learning, and Bayesian Optimization (BO).
model_or_system: Applications include bounding Bell inequalities (e.g., $I_{3322}$) and certifying ground-state energies for many-body Hamiltonians like the one-dimensional Heisenberg spin chain.
key_observables: Bound quality (gap $\Delta C$), synergy diagnostic ($\Delta(S_k)$), and convergence behavior across different Bell inequalities.
important_parameters: Computational budget (fixed resource constraint) and moment selection level ($n$ in the NPA hierarchy).
main_assumptions: The NPA relaxation sequence provides an outer approximation to the true quantum expectation value, but its computational cost grows combinatorially with the number of moments.
figures_summary: Figures compare optimization strategies (PT) for energy and observable gap certification on the Heisenberg chain, showing that warm-starting from local solutions significantly improves bounds for long-range correlations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the NPA framework, identifies moment selection as a combinatorial challenge, introduces synergy diagnostics, and then develops/compares advanced optimization algorithms (PT, RBM, BO) using quantum information benchmarks like Bell inequalities and spin chains.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial computational tool for rigorously bounding physical quantities in quantum systems where exact calculation is intractable due to high dimensionality or non-commutativity.
